canonical_name: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic for natural numbers greater than one
literal_source_claim_zh: 大于1的整数可唯一分解为素数乘积
literal_source_claim_en: Every integer greater than one can be uniquely factored as a product of primes.
canonical_statement: For every natural number n with 1 < n, there exists a finite nonempty list of prime natural numbers whose product is n, and any two lists of prime natural numbers with product n differ only by permutation.
canonical_claim: Every natural number greater than one has a finite prime factorization unique up to reordering; an equivalent unique prime-exponent form may receive credit only through a checked transport.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: For n : Nat with 1 < n, primeFactorsList n is a nonempty list of primes with product n, and every prime list with product n is a permutation of it; an exponent-map encoding is a candidate alternate form.

domain_and_universes: n : Nat in Lean universe 0, with explicit hypothesis 1 < n; factor lists contain Nat primes and uniqueness is modulo List.Perm. An Int encoding and its positive/unit transport remain uncredited.

conclusion: A prime factor list for n exists and is nonempty, and every prime factor list for n is permutation-equivalent to it.
